abstract: Niemann-Pick disease, type C (NPC) is a neurodegenerative, lysosomal storage disorder in individuals carrying two mutated copies of either the NPC1 or NPC2 gene. Consequently, impaired cholesterol recycling and an array of downstream events occur. Interestingly, in NPC, the hippocampus displays lysosomal lipid storage but does not succumb to progressive neurodegeneration as significantly as other brain regions. Since defining the neurodegeneration mechanisms in this disease is still an active area of research, we use mass spectrometry to analyze the overall proteome and phosphorylation pattern changes in the hippocampal region of a murine model of NPC. Using 3-week-old mice representing an early disease timepoint, we observed changes in the expression of 47 proteins, many of which are consistent with previous literature. New to this study, changes in members of the SNARE complex, including STX7, VTI1B, and VAMP7, were identified. Furthermore, we identified that phosphorylation of T286 on CaMKIIα and S1303 on NR2B increased in mutant animals, even at the late stage of the disease. These phosphosites are crucial to learning and memory and can trigger neuronal death by altering protein-protein interactions.
